title: The Signal That Turned Every Radio On Earth Into a Scream
hook: In 1977, a radio telescope received a signal so powerful it overwhelmed every receiver—and then every radio on Earth briefly screamed in unison.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines a mysterious cosmic event with a visceral, relatable effect (radio screaming) that feels like a horror movie.

title: The Dark Matter 'Magnet' That Dragged Earth 500 km Off Course
hook: In 2012, Earth briefly drifted 500 km from its orbital path. The cause: a dark matter clump no one saw coming.
why_this_can_go_viral: Giant, measurable planetary movement caused by something invisible taps into primal fear of unseen cosmic forces.

title: The Classified 'Gravity Bomb' That Was Tested on the Moon
hook: Declassified documents reveal a secret program that detonated a gravity-altering device on the lunar surface—and the Moon hasn't been the same since.
why_this_can_go_viral: Weaponizing gravity on the Moon is a forbidden-tech concept that triggers immediate curiosity and conspiracy intrigue.

title: The Asteroid That Hit Earth—and Came From the Future
hook: A meteorite found in Antarctica contains particles that only could have formed billions of years from now. Something sent it back.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines time travel, cosmic mystery, and a tangible object—makes the impossible feel real.

title: The Star That Blinks—and Each Blink Wipes Out a Civilization
hook: Every 1,000 years, this star dims by 20%. Astronomers calculated that each blink corresponds to the extinction of a nearby world.
why_this_can_go_viral: Linking a star's regular behavior to mass death creates an eerie, almost sentient cosmic threat.

title: The Fermi Paradox Answer: 'The Void Is Eating Them'
hook: A new model suggests advanced civilizations don't die or hide—they get absorbed by expanding voids that erase all trace of them.
why_this_can_go_viral: Gives a terrifying, novel answer to Fermi Paradox—something is actively removing civilizations from existence.

title: The Classified Space Station That Was Never Supposed to Exist
hook: A secret space station, launched in 1972, has been silently orbiting Earth for 50 years—and it's still transmitting.
why_this_can_go_viral: A hidden station from the 70s still active feels like a Cold War sci-fi plot that turned real.

title: The Asteroid That Caused Every Volcano on Earth to Erupt—Simultaneously
hook: 265 million years ago, an asteroid impact triggered all active volcanoes at once. The result: a million-year firestorm.
why_this_can_go_viral: A single event causing simultaneous global volcanic devastation is visually epic and terrifying.

title: The Ghost Planet That Orbits Our Sun—Invisible to All Instruments
hook: Astronomers detected gravitational wobbles from an invisible planet within our solar system. It's there. We just can't see it.
why_this_can_go_viral: An invisible planet in our own backyard is a classic mystery that feels like it should have been solved already.

title: The Extinction That Left No Fossils—Only Silence in the Rock
hook: Somewhere in the geological record, a mass extinction event left zero dead bodies. Life just stopped.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of an extinction so complete it erased all evidence triggers deep existential unease.

title: The Star That Is Eating Its Own Planets—One by One
hook: Astronomers watched a star swallow its innermost planet. Then it paused. Now it's hungry again.
why_this_can_go_viral: Anthropomorphizing a star as a predator makes the science instantly relatable and terrifying.

title: The Fermi Paradox 'Prison': We Are In a Walled-Off Galaxy
hook: Astronomers discovered an energy barrier at the edge of the Milky Way. Nothing leaves. Nothing enters. We are trapped.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of a cosmic prison barrier is a blockbuster-level concept that explains Fermi in the darkest way.

title: The Signal That Was a Warning—From Ourselves 10,000 Years in the Future
hook: A repeating radio pattern was decoded: it's a distress call, timestamped 12,000 AD, signed by 'Earth Council.'
why_this_can_go_viral: Time-traveling distress call from our own future is a mind-bending narrative that demands engagement.

title: The Classified Mission That Found Cities on the Dark Side of the Moon
hook: A declassified military report describes artificial structures on the lunar far side—and an order to never return.
why_this_can_go_viral: The ultimate forbidden mystery—cities on the Moon and a cover-up—is catnip for conspiracy and space fans.

title: The Dark Matter 'Storm' That Ripped a Galaxy in Half
hook: A galaxy was found split into two halves, still connected by a bridge of dark matter. The storm isn't over.
why_this_can_go_viral: The visual of a galaxy ripped apart by invisible dark matter is both scientifically fascinating and terrifying.

title: The 'Supermoon' That Almost Tore Earth's Crust Open
hook: In 2011, the Moon's closest approach in 18 years nearly triggered a crust fracture. A few meters closer and Earth would have split.

title: The Star That Turned Into a Black Hole—But Kept Shining for 10 Years
hook: A star collapsed into a black hole, but its light persisted for a decade. It was emitting from beyond the event horizon.
why_this_can_go_viral: Defies known physics—a star that 'should be dead' still burning—creates intense curiosity and mystery.

title: The Extinction That Was Caused by a Molecular Cloud—We Passed Through It
hook: Earth once drifted into a dark molecular cloud that compressed the heliosphere and let cosmic rays sterilize the surface.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea that Earth passed through an invisible space poison is a fresh, scientific horror scenario.

title: The Asteroid That Is 'Shadowing' Earth—Matching Our Orbit Exactly
hook: An asteroid the size of a mountain is flying in perfect lockstep with Earth, always staying 30 degrees behind. It's been there for centuries.
why_this_can_go_viral: A stealth asteroid permanently tailing Earth feels like a cosmic stalker—deeply unsettling and intriguing.

title: The Classified 'Echo' Program That Broadcast Our Location to the Galaxy
hook: In the 1960s, a secret military project beamed a message into deep space. But the recipient wasn't specified—and it was too late to cancel.
why_this_can_go_viral: We accidentally announced our presence to the galaxy—and now we can't take it back. Classic sci-fi horror.
